title: Republic of Vietnam
capsule: South Vietnam, formally the Republic of Vietnam (Việt Nam Cộng hòa), was the anti-communist state established in 1955 in the territory south of the 17th parallel after the 1954 Geneva Accords partitioned Vietnam. Led first by Ngô Đình Diệm and sustained by United States aid, it faced a growing communist insurgency by the Viet Cong backed from the North, which drew American combat forces into the Vietnam War from 1965. Chronic instability followed Diệm’s assassination in 1963; after the U.S. withdrawal under the 1973 Paris Peace Accords, the North’s 1975 offensive captured Saigon, ending the republic and leading to reunification in 1976.
